LESSON: READING 8.2.1 FLUENCY IN READING

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What makes someone a good reader?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify unfamiliar words in texts for fluency
2. read a text accurately, with expression and at the right speed for fluency

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: READING 8.2.1 FLUENCY IN READING
This lesson teaches Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading for Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify unfamiliar words in texts for fluency
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. read a text accurately, with expression and at the right speed for fluency
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading above.
2. Explain Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 8.2.1 Fluency in Reading important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What makes someone a good reader?
2. How long do you take to read a text?
3. What can you do to improve your reading speed?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify unfamiliar words in texts for fluency
2. read a text accurately, with expression and at the right speed for fluency

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
